correctness.rationale: For 0<tau<1 and all two-visit phase separations, isotropic orbital orientation gives uniform line of sight. Two signed antipodal caps per epoch reduce nondetection to exactly four disjoint equal-cap overlaps. A spherical-triangle construction yields L_alpha(s) and direct differentiation gives L_prime=-2 sqrt(1-h^2/cos^2(s/2)) for s<2alpha. This derivative magnitude strictly decreases, proving all optimal-delay and equality cases; the two-vector eigenvalue bound gives the sharp worst-orientation guarantee. A near-tangency integral gives the 3/2 onset with stated coefficient. Independently sampled spherical-grid event frequencies and 7584 finite checker assertions corroborate selected boundaries and identities but are not substituted for infinite proofs. Assumptions, equality convention, and instrumental limitations are explicit.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Broader stochastic simulation and numerical optimization cover the physical scenario as a computational special case, so the event and numerical probability are prior art. Those methods alone do not state or establish the exact analytic optimizer, its full equality set, worst-orientation bound, or 3/2 critical onset. The new theorem has deliberately restricted hypotheses and does not claim to dominate realistic mission optimization.

originality.rationale: The source papers establish direct imaging observability, circular-orbit geometry and even numerical multi-visit optimization. The narrower contribution is an explicit all-parameter analytic two-visit probability, a global optimal phase diagram with equality sets, a uniform worst-case separation bound, and a 3/2 incompleteness onset. Four highly relevant accessible primary texts and relevant mathematical records were compared at the level of implication rather than keywords. A generic cap-area formula and numerical completeness algorithm are correctly acknowledged; historical equivalence remains a residual risk rather than a manufactured uniqueness guarantee.
residual_risks: Earlier work on spherical antipodal cap overlaps may contain an equivalent global optimality statement in general geometric language; no such covering theorem was located in the inspected results.
Realistic multi-visit astrophysical scheduling algorithms numerically subsume this ideal scenario but do not provide its exact displayed expression and threshold in inspected text.
The result intentionally excludes brightness and exposure-time costs, so the operational quarter-period rule is not universal for actual instruments.
Independent literature and proof audit have not been performed.

value.rationale: Astronomical direct imaging explicitly uses inner working angle, random inclinations, and timed revisits. For a fixed circular orbit and IWA-only detection, it is a natural design question whether a second observation can guarantee discovery and what delay maximizes completeness. The theorem supplies an exact all-parameter solution, identifies a genuine guaranteed-detection phase versus an unavoidable-miss phase and its sharp 3/2 boundary, and gives quantitative probability gains without Monte Carlo. This is a motivated complete classification of a fundamental ideal observation setting, though it does not imply a scheduling rule with contrast, eccentricity, or real operational costs.
